output: html_document
---
```{r}
library(brms)
library(tidyverse)

# Create a directory to save plots
dir.create("glm_plots", showWarnings = FALSE)

# Helper function to save ggplot
save_plot <- function(plot, name) {
  ggsave(paste0("glm_plots/", name, ".png"), plot, width = 6, height = 4)
}

# 1. Poisson Regression (Count Data)
set.seed(1)
df_poisson <- tibble(x = rnorm(100)) %>%
  mutate(y = rpois(100, lambda = exp(0.5 + 0.3 * x)))

model_poisson <- brm(y ~ x, family = poisson(), data = df_poisson, chains = 2, iter = 1000)
plot_poisson <- ggplot(df_poisson, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "glm", method.args = list(family = "poisson"), se = FALSE) +
  ggtitle("Poisson Regression")
save_plot(plot_poisson, "poisson")

# 2. Logistic Regression (Binary Outcome)
df_logistic <- tibble(x = rnorm(100)) %>%
  mutate(p = plogis(-0.5 + 1.5 * x),
         y = rbinom(100, 1, p))

model_logistic <- brm(y ~ x, family = bernoulli(), data = df_logistic, chains = 2, iter = 1000)
plot_logistic <- ggplot(df_logistic, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_point(position = position_jitter(height = 0.05)) +
  geom_smooth(method = "glm", method.args = list(family = "binomial"), se = FALSE) +
  ggtitle("Logistic Regression")
save_plot(plot_logistic, "logistic")

# 3. Negative Binomial (Overdispersion)
df_nb <- tibble(x = rnorm(100)) %>%
  mutate(y = rnbinom(100, mu = exp(0.5 + 0.3 * x), size = 1))

model_nb <- brm(y ~ x, family = negbinomial(), data = df_nb, chains = 2, iter = 1000)
plot_nb <- ggplot(df_nb, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_point() +
  ggtitle("Negative Binomial Regression")
save_plot(plot_nb, "negative_binomial")

# 4. Gamma Regression (Skewed Duration)
df_gamma <- tibble(x = rnorm(100)) %>%
  mutate(y = rgamma(100, shape = 2, rate = exp(-0.5 - 0.3 * x)))

model_gamma <- brm(y ~ x, family = Gamma("log"), data = df_gamma, chains = 2, iter = 1000)
plot_gamma <- ggplot(df_gamma, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_point() +
  ggtitle("Gamma Regression")
save_plot(plot_gamma, "gamma")

# 5. ExGaussian Regression (Skewed RT)
df_exgauss <- tibble(x = rnorm(100)) %>%
  mutate(y = rexgaussian(100, mu = 2 + x, sigma = 0.5, tau = 1))

model_exgauss <- brm(y ~ x, family = exgaussian(), data = df_exgauss, chains = 2, iter = 1000)
plot_exgauss <- ggplot(df_exgauss, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_point() +
  ggtitle("ExGaussian Regression")
save_plot(plot_exgauss, "exgaussian")

# 6. Ordered Logistic (Likert Data)
df_ordinal <- tibble(x = rnorm(100)) %>%
  mutate(score = cut_number(x + rnorm(100), n = 5, labels = FALSE))

model_ordinal <- brm(score ~ x, family = cumulative(), data = df_ordinal, chains = 2, iter = 1000)
plot_ordinal <- ggplot(df_ordinal, aes(x, score)) +
  geom_jitter(height = 0.2) +
  ggtitle("Ordered Logistic Regression")
save_plot(plot_ordinal, "ordered_logistic")

# 7. Beta Regression (Proportion Rating)
df_beta <- tibble(x = rnorm(100)) %>%
  mutate(p = plogis(0.5 * x),
         y = rbeta(100, shape1 = p * 10, shape2 = (1 - p) * 10))

model_beta <- brm(y ~ x, family = Beta(), data = df_beta, chains = 2, iter = 1000)
plot_beta <- ggplot(df_beta, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_point() +
  ggtitle("Beta Regression")
save_plot(plot_beta, "beta")

# 8. Distributional Regression (Model Mean + Variance)
df_dist <- tibble(x = rnorm(100)) %>%
  mutate(sd = 0.5 + 0.3 * abs(x),
         y = rnorm(100, mean = 2 + x, sd = sd))

model_dist <- brm(bf(y ~ x, sigma ~ x), data = df_dist, chains = 2, iter = 1000)
plot_dist <- ggplot(df_dist, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_point() +
  ggtitle("Distributional Regression (Mean + Variance)")
save_plot(plot_dist, "distributional")

```
